recipes.name: Dallas-Style Sloppy Joes
ingredients_raw: sea salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Cook the ground beef in a large skillet over medium heat until completely browned, 5 to 7 minutes. Add the onion and bell pepper, season with sea salt and black pepper, and cook until vegetables soften, about 7 minutes.

Stir in the ketchup, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, brown sugar, mustard, and barbeque sauce. Reduce heat to low and simmer the mixture until thickened, about 10 minutes. Add Parmesan cheese and serve on toasted hamburger buns.

raw_recipe.headline: Dallas-Style Sloppy Joes
raw_recipe.description: A zesty sauce, fresh onion, and bell pepper make this easy-to-make sandwich a Dallas-area favorite.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe! The family loved it! It's quick and easy. The only things I changed was due to it being too tangy I added 1/4 cup white granulated sugar, I omitted the salt and worcestershire sauce and added 1 tablespoon minced garlic instead. I let it simmer for about 45 mins and it turned out great! Thanks for a great recipe...I will be making this again!

This is great. my wife and i like things a little hotter so i tweaked it a little. we added 1 chopped jalepeño to the veggies. I left the liquid in to help soften the veggies and then drained (which i didnt see in the original instructions). i used 85/15 beef. i added 1 tsp of cayenne pepper. only 1.25 cups of ketchup and 1/4 cup of Sweet Baby Rays sweet and spicy sauce. Finally we added sharp cheddar cheese. Great taste and even better the next day.

These were very tasty, very saucy, almost too saucey though... I had to simmer this 45 min to get it reduced/thickened. Plus it needed the time for the flavor to develop. Tangy flavor, zesty with some zing but not too spicy, or sweet or tomatoey, a nice blend of all. I scaled this back to 1 lb of beef. I used 2 Tbl dried minced onion and 2 heaping Tbl. of diced pimento pepper in the jar, Head Country bbq sauce, which didn't have hickory so I put in a couple of drops of mesquite liquid smoke (the only kind I had on hand). I used about a half tsp of sea salt, 1/4 tsp celery salt, and 5 or 6 grinds of black pepper and a tsp of paprika to go with the pimento since I didn't use fresh sweet red pepper. I buttered the buns and grilled them til they were toasty and golden, topped with sloppy joe filling and a slice of american cheese, this made a nice filling lunch and I had plenty of leftovers for another meal. ***These were even better after I reheated the leftovers. I almost gave this a 5 based on what I reheated, but the original recipe only says to cook these a few minutes and they certainly would not really compare with my final product. Fabulous recipe, I'll certainly use this again. Thanks so much for posting this one!

Along with all the ingredients listed I added 1 can of diced Tomatoes & only used 1-Cup Ketchup. I also only used 1-lb Hamburger and replaced the yellow onion with dried minced onion about 2 tbsp. Added some green peppers (1/4 C), black pepper, a few drops of Tone's Liquid Smoke. Added a little water and just simmered away for a long time until thick. Yum Yum.

My family loved this recipe!! The only thing I did different was add extra of everything because I used 3lbs of meat to feed all 6 of us. I cooked it on my electric skillet, which cooks pretty fast and that's always good! I also added a little bit of chili powder just for a kick. I will definitely be making this again!!
Delicious! The red pepper was so good in this. I only used about 1 cup ketchup because that's all I had, but will do so again, because the sauce came out thick--not too "sloppy" and very flavorful.

We like a less ketchup-y sauce, so I used half hickory smoke barbeque sauce and half ketchup. I also added a tsp. of Liquid Smoke and I used dijon instead of yellow mustard. I also added 8 cloves minced garlic. My boys really liked these. I liked how these were less sloppy than your usual sloppy joes. They held together well, which a Mother appreciates. NOTE: The parmesan cheese was a nice touch. I didn't bother using the snooty kind, just plain old Kraft. This made quite a bit, filled eight big buns and there was enough for my husband's lunch tomorrow. Maybe ten servings, two small sized.
My family loved it! It was so quick and easy. Even though we all like the tang from the vinegar, I think that I will back it down to 2 1/2 tblsp. the next time.
My family thought this was great. I will leave the brown sugar out next time as it was very sweet but otherwise it was very good.

This was good but needed some changes. I found it too sweet. Will cut down brown sugar to 1 Tbsp. I cut down the Ketchup to 1/2 cup and even that was a bit much. I increased the Worcestershire sauce and barbecue sauce. My husband loved it.

Yummy flavors! I used 1 tbsp of tomato paste & 1 sm can of tomato sauce with 3 tbsp of ketchup. Then used 1 tbsp of each of the remaining ingredients except BBQ sauce which I used 1.5 tbsps. I also used a green pepper in place of the red. Definitely will make again!!

I enjoyed this recipe, I did not have the red bell pepper, so I left that out, but the other ingredients I had in the house. I used cheddar cheese on top instead of Parmesan. I like spicy food, hubby does not but he also enjoyed it. It is not overly spicy. I served it on garlic bread. At 530 calories per serving, I won't be making this often, but it is a nice treat.
Delicious recipe.
This is delish and simple. Left out the parm, otherwise everything else kept the same. Came out perfect!
Went over well. Family loved it so much the next night left overs where the meal of choice!
Excellent recipe. Same recipe we had in middle school home ec.
GREAT tangy and delightful
Very Good!!!
I have made this several times now and we really enjoy it. We like the tangy flavor. Thanks for posting the recipe!
